A page's own script on a map

Source: R/script.R
og_script.Rd

og_script() puts a script of your own (and its styles) into the map's page, for what the layer functions do not do: a panel of your own, a click that does something else, data sent again as the reader works. It runs once the map's layers are added, given one object, og, the whole of what it may use of the page (anything else of the page, its elements and functions, may change from one version to the next):

Usage

og_script(map, js, css = NULL)

Arguments

map

An og_map().

js

The script: the path of a .js file, or the script itself as text.

css

Its styles, optionally: the path of a .css file, or the styles as text.

Value

The map, with the script.

Details

  • og.map: MapLibre's map.

  • og.layer(id): a layer's MapLibre style ids, source and key, by its id (og_point()'s id and the others'), or null. A layer function's features are known by their row's number (key "og_row", MapLibre's feature id: a click's feature.id); a layer of your own by its og_layer()'s key.

  • og.state(id, key, value): a feature's state in MapLibre (setFeatureState()), by its layer and key, which its styles read as list("feature-state", "<name>") (given to a layer function in MapLibre's own terms, ...): a selection drawn with no data sent again. og.state(id, key) reads it, og.state(id, key, null) clears it; it is kept through a change of base map.

  • og.on("click", id, fn): a click on the layer's features is the script's: fn({feature, lngLat, point, row}), where row() is a promise of the clicked row's columns (those its popup names, each name, label, unit, value), or null when the reader has clicked again meanwhile; the layer's own popup is not shown.

  • og.setData(id, geojson): a layer sent whole (whole = TRUE) given new data, at most once a frame.

  • og.filter(id, key, expr): a filter of the script's on a layer (a MapLibre expression), kept with the page's own choices; null removes it.

  • og.panel(title): a box in the sidebar, the script's to fill (its body element).

  • og.fetch(name, init): the map's own route name (og_serve()'s routes), as fetch(); after the name, a path and a query as written, for the route's path and query ("marks/12?full=1"; a value made safe with encodeURIComponent(), or the query with URLSearchParams). og.served is false in a bundle, which has no server.

  • og.save(name, text): a file handed to the reader to save, which a page in a bundle keeps in place of a server.

A map with a script is written into a bundle (og_bundle()) with it, where it runs with no R: og.fetch() is refused there and og.save() keeps what the reader made.

See also

og_serve() for the map's own routes.

Examples

# \donttest{
# a click on a position lists its vessel and time in a panel of the script's own
js <- r"(
  const body = og.panel("Clicked");
  og.on("click", "positions", async ({ row }) => {
    const r = await row();
    if (r) body.append(Object.assign(document.createElement("div"),
                       { textContent: r.map(c => c.value).join(" · ") }));
  });
)"
m <- og_example("trawlsurvey") |>
  og_point(id = "positions", popup = c(vid, time)) |>
  og_script(js)
# }
